football_evidence.question: Can Kennesaw State contain Delaware’s explosive runs?
football_evidence.assessment: No material disagreement: EdgeDesk and the line are within 0.7 points.
supporting: When Delaware has the ball (big plays on the ground): Delaware’s offense turns 3.3% of its runs into explosive gains, and Kennesaw State’s defense gives up explosive gains on 3.0% of opponent runs (FBS average 6.5%).

When Kennesaw State has the ball (early downs): Kennesaw State’s offense succeeds on 43.0% of its first- and second-down plays, and Delaware’s defense allows success on 52.3% of first- and second-down plays (FBS average 42.5%).

When Delaware has the ball (the line of scrimmage on running plays): Delaware’s offense is stopped at or behind the line on 21.6% of its runs, and Kennesaw State’s defense stops 16.7% of opponent runs at or behind the line (FBS average 17.5%).
EdgeDesk’s position-group ratings put Kennesaw State’s defensive line No. 53 nationally and Delaware’s No. 120.
contradicting: When Kennesaw State has the ball (pass protection against the pass rush): Kennesaw State’s offense has allowed a sack on 4.5% of its dropbacks, and Delaware’s defense sacks the quarterback on 8.9% of opponent dropbacks (FBS average 5.7%).

When Delaware has the ball (pass protection against the pass rush): Delaware’s offense has allowed a sack on 7.4% of its dropbacks, and Kennesaw State’s defense sacks the quarterback on 2.3% of opponent dropbacks (FBS average 5.7%).

When Delaware has the ball (big plays through the air): Delaware’s offense turns 14.2% of its pass plays into explosive gains, and Kennesaw State’s defense gives up explosive gains on 9.4% of opponent pass plays (FBS average 10.2%).
